headline: Pentagon launches custom ChatGPT and Grok for 3 million personnel
summary: The Department of Defense has rolled out secure, tailored versions of OpenAI's ChatGPT and xAI's Grok, aiming to boost capabilities for its 3 million civilian and military staff.
details: The Pentagon has officially launched custom versions of OpenAI's ChatGPT and xAI's Grok, integrating them into its GenAI.mil portal. These AI tools are specifically adapted for "warfighter needs," providing secure access to generative AI for over 3 million personnel.

GenAI.mil, initially launched with Google Gemini, serves as a secure platform enabling Department of Defense employees to utilize commercial AI models without risking sensitive government data. The military-specific versions are designed to avoid the data collection common in consumer AI products.

The generative AI portal has seen significant adoption, with more than 1.7 million unique users already onboarded out of the department's 3 million personnel. This highlights the growing reliance on AI for accelerating work and enhancing operational efficiency.

ChatGPT Mil, developed through OpenAI's Government program, will offer familiar features like chat, file analysis, and custom GPTs. It is intended to support unclassified tasks such as administrative duties, logistics, planning, and policy development.

Grok for Government, provided by Starshield AI (SpaceX's secure satellite network), is positioned for broader military applications. The Department of Defense states it will offer "immediate productivity gains, stronger knowledge continuity and more secure and efficient collaboration" for warfighters.

The Pentagon anticipates Grok will enable military personnel to execute missions faster and with greater precision. Potential uses range from market research analysis for acquisition professionals to supply chain management for logisticians.

These advancements are part of a larger Pentagon strategy to leverage AI for a strategic edge, while maintaining stringent security protocols. The absence of Anthropic's Claude model from the portal is noted, following past disputes over safety guardrails and data usage.
